text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CARDOSO JOINS THE BATTLE FOR RE-ELECTION

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso is to meet the governor of Pernambuco state Wednesday to discuss the constitutional amendment which would allow Cardoso to run for a second term if approved by Congress.
-- FARMERS WILL HAVE TO DECLARE UNDER NEW TAX RULES
Brazilian landowners with farms of more than 500 hectares will have to declare in detail how much of their land is currently being used for agricultural purposes.
O GLOBO
-- WOMAN KIDNAPS BABY FROM MATERNITY WARD
A woman disguised as a nurse has kidnapped a 48-hour-old baby from the maternity ward of a Rio de Janeiro hospital.
-- DRUG TRAFFICKERS CHOOSE SAMBA SCHOOL'S CARNIVAL SONG
Drug traffickers from two favelas decided to which samba song the Unidos de Vila Isabel samba school will dance at the 1997 Rio de Janeiro carnival.
-- MOST MAYORS ELECTED IN RIO STATE COME FROM PSDB PARTY
Most mayors elected in Rio de Janeiro state in last week's municipal elections belong to the PSDB party.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- SAO PAULO GOVERNOR ATTACKS RE-ELECTION DEAL WITH MALUF

Sao Paulo state governor Mario Covas has criticized the federal government for supporting in the second round of voting the mayoral candidate backed by the city's mayor Paulo Maluf in exchange for Maluf's support for presidential re-election.
-- NUMBER OF NON-VOTERS GROWS IN SAO PAULO
The number of eligible voters in Sao Paulo who did not vote in last week's municipal elections has risen to 16.4 percent from 11.3 percent four years ago.
-- 54 PRISONERS ESCAPE FROM SAO PAULO POLICE STATION
Fifty four prisoners escaped on Sunday from a police station in the south of Sao Paulo which closes on weekends.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
